questions.question: What is crossover? Explain its role in Genetic Algorithms.
questions.solution_html:
• What is crossover? Explain its role in Genetic Algorithms.
  • Crossover is a genetic operator that combines genetic information from two parent chromosomes to
  • produce new offspring in a Genetic Algorithm (GA).
  • Role of crossover:
  • • Combines useful characteristics of different parents.
  • • Introduces new combinations of solutions.
  • • Helps explore the search space.
  • • May improve the quality of solutions over successive generations.

questions.question: What is the basic difference between Bagging and Boosting? / [CO2, CO3, CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• What is the basic difference between Bagging and Boosting?
  • Bagging Boosting
  • Stands for Bootstrap Aggregating. Combines learners sequentially to improve performance.
  • Models are trained independently,
  • often in parallel.
  • Models are trained sequentially, with later learners
  • responding to earlier errors or residuals.
  • Uses bootstrap samples of the
  • training data.
  • Commonly changes sample weights or fits residuals,
  • depending on the algorithm.
  • Combines predictions using voting
  • or averaging. Combines learners using a weighted or additive prediction.
  • Primarily reduces variance. Often reduces bias and can also reduce variance.
  • Example: Random Forest. Examples: AdaBoost and Gradient Boosting.

questions.question: Compare L1 and L2 regularization methods.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare L1 and L2 regularization methods.
  • Regularization is a technique used in machine learning to reduce overfitting by making the model
  • simpler and improving its performance on new data.
  • L1 Regularization (Lasso Regression)
  • • Also called Lasso Regression.
  • • Adds the absolute value of the coefficients as a penalty to the loss function.
  • • Shrinks some coefficients exactly to zero, effectively removing less important features.
  • • Useful for feature selection, especially when there are many features.
  • L2 Regularization (Ridge Regression)
  • • Also called Ridge Regression.
  • • Adds the square of the coefficients as a penalty to the loss function.
  • • Reduces the size of coefficients but does not make them zero.
  • • Keeps all features while reducing their influence, helping prevent overfitting.

questions.question: Classify independence and conditional independence in probability- based intelligent agents.
questions.solution_html:
• Classify independence and conditional independence in probability-based intelligent agents.
  • • Independence – definition and equation: (4 marks) .
  • • Conditional independence – definition and equation: (4 marks)
  • • Suitable example for each: (2 marks)
  • Independence: Two events (A) and (B) are independent if (P(A,B)=P(A)P(B)). The occurrence of
  • one event does not affect the probability of the other.
  • -Conditional Independence: Two events (A) and (B) are conditionally independent given (C) if
  • (P(A,B| C)=P(A| C)P(B| C)\). Given (C), knowing one event provides no additional information
  • about the other.
